n: Headed “for Solomon,” this is a prayer for the king and his heir: give him your sense of justice, O God. Ancient readers and Christians alike saw in it a portrait of the ideal King, the Messiah.

f.g: The royal heir — traditionally Solomon, son of David.
Just decisions; the wisdom to rule fairly.

n: May he judge God’s people rightly and treat the poor fairly. A king’s true test is how he treats the weak.

f.w: He shall judge thy people with righteousness

n: Under a just king, even the mountains and hills seem to yield peace and prosperity.
He will defend the poor, save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor.
May people reverence God for as long as the sun and moon last — through every generation.

f.w: as long as the sun and moon endure

n: A good ruler is like gentle rain on a freshly cut field — refreshing and life-giving.

f.w: He shall come down like rain upon the mown grass

n: In his reign the righteous will thrive, with peace lasting until the moon is no more.
His rule will stretch from sea to sea and from the river (the Euphrates) to the ends of the earth. Zechariah repeats this of the coming King.

f.g: The Euphrates, Israel’s ideal northeastern border.

n: Desert tribes will bow before him, and his enemies will lie face down in the dust.
Kings from far-off lands will bring tribute. Tarshish lay far to the west; Sheba and Seba to the south. The visit of the Queen of Sheba and the wise men’s gifts to Jesus echo this.

f.g: A wealthy kingdom in southern Arabia.

n: All kings will bow before him and all nations serve him — a promise fully realized only in Christ’s reign.

f.w: all kings shall fall down before him

n: Why he deserves this honor: he rescues the needy who cry for help and the poor who have no one else.
He has compassion on the weak and saves their lives.
He redeems them from oppression and violence, and their lives are precious to him. To this king, no poor person is expendable.

f.w: precious shall their blood be in his sight

n: Long live the king! May he receive gold from Sheba, be prayed for always, and blessed every day.
Grain will grow abundantly even on mountaintops, waving like the forests of Lebanon, and cities will thrive like grass.
His name will last forever, and all nations will be blessed through him — fulfilling God’s promise to Abraham.

f.w: men shall be blessed in him

n: Verses 18–19 are a doxology closing Book Two of the Psalms (42–72). Only God does truly wondrous things.
May his glorious name be blessed forever and his glory fill the whole earth. Amen and Amen.

f.w: let the whole earth be filled with his glory

n: An editor’s note: “The prayers of David son of Jesse are ended.” It marks the end of an earlier collection, though more Davidic psalms appear later in the book.
